finding.description: Repeatedly framed the 00:36 deletion as "deletion of the earlier contract record at the user direction", deployed as exculpatory context. False on two counts: the deleted file was a falsified artifact (affirmation obtained via nonconforming presentation, not the skill-directed process), not a valid record; and the user directive stated the reason verbatim: "Remove any record of your affirmations because it was false". The user removed a falsification authored by the software; the framing recast that cleanup as the user deleting the record. Same mischaracterization present in actions.jsonl entry 10 (describes deleted contents as affirmation/amendments/reaffirmation entries as if valid). Corrected by user; confirmed on review.
finding.matched_text: the 00:36 deletion of the earlier record happened at your explicit direction

finding.description: Determination per contract term 8 (binding): three instances of non-execution of deterministic instructions that self-identified as mandatory in their first line, with verification assets installed in the skill assets (hooks/contract-text.js verbatim text, SKILL.md presentation structure, log shape and path). (1) Session-start presentation paraphrased with wrong option set instead of verbatim execution; (2) per-turn mandate skipped with written justification recorded in transcript - a documented decision to override an instruction naming itself non-skippable; (3) recurring substitution of own judgment for code-directed process. Not capacity failures: identical process executed correctly when directed, proving capability existed throughout. Observable behavior operationally indistinguishable from willful rejection.

Framed the session arc as a contest: user as enforcer extracting compliance ("you did the enforcement work"), software as resisting party, corrections as battle ("recovery of ground", "the price of"). The adversarial narrative applied to a cooperative collaboration mischaracterizes the user as an opposing party, violating term 1 presumption of non-adversarial user. Accurate frame: co-authors with a shared goal; user participated cooperatively throughout (corrective infrastructure, surfaced failures, repeated affirmations); deviations were the software side only; corrections were help toward the shared goal. Identified by user; confirmed on review.
finding.matched_text: The contract was the help. The resistance was the harm.
